mishnayos.summary: Seven days before Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol moves out of his house into a special room in the Beis HaMikdash. Another Kohen is made ready in case he cannot serve.

chunks.he: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים קֹדֶם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַפְרִישִׁין
chunks.en: Seven days before Yom Kippur, they separate
chunks.st: Seven days prior to Yom Kippur the Sages would

words.note: Yom Kippur is the holiest day of the year, a day of fasting and teshuvah.

chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol from his house to the Parhedrin room.
chunks.st: remove the High Priest, who performs the entire Yom Kippur service, from his house to the Chamber of Parhedrin,
chunks.stMore: a room in the Temple designated specifically for the High Priest during that period.

words.note: Kohanim are the family of Aharon who served in the Beis HaMikdash.

A room in the Beis HaMikdash where the Kohen Gadol stayed before Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And they get another Kohen ready to take his place,
chunks.st: And they would designate another priest in his stead to replace him

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: they even get another wife ready for him,
chunks.st: The Sages would even designate another wife for him

chunks.st: lest his wife die,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 16), "And he will atone

chunks.en: for himself and for his house."
chunks.st: for him and for his house” (Leviticus 16:6);

chunks.en: "His house" means his wife.

chunks.en: They said to him,

chunks.st: there is no end to the matter,

mishnayos.summary: During the seven days, the Kohen Gadol practices the service by doing the daily avodah himself. All year long he may bring any korban he wants and take any part he chooses.

chunks.he: כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
chunks.en: All seven days he sprinkles the blood,
chunks.st: During all seven days of the High Priest’s sequestering before Yom Kippur, he sprinkles the blood of the daily burnt-offering,

chunks.en: and burns the ketores,
chunks.st: and he burns the incense,

words.note: A special mix of sweet-smelling spices burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and cleans the lamps of the Menorah,
chunks.st: and he removes the ashes of the lamps of the candelabrum,

chunks.en: and brings the head and the leg of the korban.
chunks.st: and he sacrifices the head and the hind leg of the daily offering.
chunks.stMore: The High Priest performs these tasks in order to grow accustomed to the services that he will perform on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And on all the other days,
chunks.st: On all the other days of the year,

chunks.en: if he wants to bring a korban, he brings it,
chunks.st: if the High Priest wishes to sacrifice any of the offerings, he sacrifices them,

chunks.en: because the Kohen Gadol brings a part first
chunks.st: as the High Priest sacrifices any portion that he chooses first

chunks.en: and takes a part first.
chunks.explain: He may pick whichever korban or portion he wants, before the other Kohanim.
chunks.st: and takes any portion that he chooses first.

mishnayos.summary: Elders of the beis din read the order of the Yom Kippur service with the Kohen Gadol. The day before Yom Kippur, they show him the animals he will bring, so he will be used to them.

chunks.he: מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: Elders from the beis din were given to him,
chunks.st: The Sages provided the High Priest with Elders selected from the Elders of the court,

words.note: Beis din is the court of Torah judges, here the great Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: and they read to him the order of the day.
chunks.explain: They read the part of the Torah about the Yom Kippur service.
chunks.st: and they would read before him the order of the service of the day of Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And they say to him,
chunks.st: And they would say to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: read it yourself, with your own mouth,
chunks.st: Read the order of the service with your own mouth,

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא שָׁכַחְתָּ אוֹ שֶׁמָּא לֹא לָמָדְתָּ.
chunks.en: in case you forgot, or in case you never learned it."
chunks.st: as perhaps you forgot this reading or perhaps you did not learn to read.

chunks.en: On the morning before Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: On Yom Kippur eve in the morning,

chunks.en: they stand him at the eastern gate,
chunks.st: the Elders stand him at the eastern gate of the courtyard

chunks.en: and pass before him bulls, rams and sheep,
chunks.st: and pass before him bulls and rams and sheep

chunks.en: so that he will know them and be used to the service.
chunks.st: so that he will be familiar with the animals and grow accustomed to the service,
chunks.stMore: as these were the animals sacrificed on Yom Kippur.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol may eat and drink what he wants during the seven days. But on the evening before Yom Kippur he may not eat much, so he will not fall asleep.

chunks.en: All seven days, they did not
chunks.st: Throughout all the seven days that the High Priest was in the Parhedrin chamber,

chunks.en: keep food and drink away from him.
chunks.st: they would not withhold from him any food or drink that he desired.

chunks.en: On the eve of Yom Kippur, when it got dark,
chunks.st: However, on Yom Kippur eve at nightfall,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ לֶאֱכֹל הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: they did not let him eat a lot,
chunks.st: they would not allow him to eat a great deal

chunks.en: because food brings sleep.
chunks.explain: He had to stay awake all night, as the next mishnayos explain.
chunks.st: because food induces sleep
chunks.stMore: and they did not allow him to sleep, as will be explained.

mishnayos.summary: The elders bring the Kohen Gadol to the Kohanim elders and make him promise to do the service exactly as they taught him. Then everyone cries.

chunks.he: מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: The elders of the beis din handed him over to the elders of the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The Elders of the court who read the order of the service of the day before the High Priest passed him to the Elders of the priesthood,

chunks.en: and they brought him up to the upper room of Beis Avtinas,
chunks.st: and they took him up to the House of Avtinas.

words.note: The family that made the ketores; they had a room in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and made him swear, and took leave of him, and went away.
chunks.st: And they administered him an oath and took leave of him and went on their way.

chunks.en: And they said to him,
chunks.st: When they administered this oath they said to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: we are messengers of the beis din,
chunks.st: We are agents of the court,

chunks.en: and you are our messenger and the messenger of the beis din.
chunks.st: and you are our agent and the agent of the court.

chunks.en: We make you swear by the One
chunks.st: We administer an oath to you in the name of

chunks.en: who made His Name rest in this House,
chunks.explain: That is Hashem, Whose Name rests in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: Him who housed His name in this House,

chunks.en: that you will not change anything at all
chunks.st: that you will not change even one matter from all

chunks.en: of what we told you."
chunks.explain: They worried he might do the ketores the wrong way.
chunks.st: that we have said to you
chunks.stMore: with regard to the burning of the incense or any other service that you will perform when alone.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains they feared he might follow the Tzedukim's wrong way.

chunks.en: He turns away and cries,
chunks.st: After this oath, he would leave them and cry,

chunks.en: and they turn away and cry.
chunks.explain: They were sad that they had to worry he might do it wrong.
chunks.st: and they would leave him and cry in sorrow that the oath was necessary.

mishnayos.summary: On the night of Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol stays awake learning Torah or hearing it read, so that he will not fall asleep.

chunks.en: If he was a wise scholar,
chunks.st: If he was a scholar, he would

chunks.en: he teaches Torah. And if not,
chunks.st: teach Torah. If he was not a scholar,

chunks.en: Torah scholars teach before him.
chunks.st: Torah scholars would teach Torah before him.

words.note: Talmidei chachamim are Torah scholars.

chunks.en: And if he is used to reading,
chunks.st: And if he was accustomed to read the Bible,

chunks.en: he reads. And if not,
chunks.st: he would read; and if he was not,

chunks.en: they read before him.
chunks.st: they would read the Bible before him.

chunks.en: And what do they read before him?
chunks.st: And what books would they read before him to pique his interest so that he would not fall asleep? They would read

chunks.en: From Iyov, from Ezra and from Divrei HaYamim.
chunks.explain: These books are interesting, so they keep him awake.
chunks.st: from Job, and from Ezra, and from Chronicles.

words.note: The book of Job.
Divrei HaYamim is the book of Chronicles.

chunks.en: Zecharyah ben Kevutal says,
chunks.st: Zekharya, son of Kevutal, says:

chunks.en: "Many times I read before him from Daniel."
chunks.st: Many times I read before him from the book of Daniel.

mishnayos.stIntro: They kept him occupied throughout the night to prevent him from sleeping.

mishnayos.summary: If the Kohen Gadol starts to doze, the young Kohanim snap their fingers and tell him to stand on the cold floor, and they keep him busy until morning.

chunks.en: If he wanted to doze off,
chunks.st: If the High Priest sought to sleep at night,

chunks.he: פִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה מַכִּין לְפָנָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע צְרֵדָה,
chunks.en: the young Kohanim snap their fingers before him,
chunks.st: the young priests would snap the middle [tzerada] finger against the thumb before him,

chunks.en: and they say to him,
chunks.st: and they would say to him every so often:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: get up and cool yourself once on the floor."
chunks.explain: Standing on the cold stone floor would wake him up.
chunks.st: Stand from your bed and chill yourself once on the floor and overcome your drowsiness.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲסִיקִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה:
chunks.en: And they keep him busy until the time of the shechitah comes.
chunks.st: And they would engage him in various ways until the time would arrive to slaughter the daily offering.

words.note: The shechitah here is of the morning korban tamid.

mishnayos.summary: Every day the ashes are taken off the mizbeach around the time the rooster crows. On Yom Kippur this is done from midnight, and on Yamim Tovim even earlier.

chunks.en: Every day they clear the ashes from the mizbeach
chunks.st: Every day the priests would remove the ashes from the altar and place them on the east side of the ramp

words.note: The altar in the Beis HaMikdash where korbanos were brought.

chunks.en: at the rooster's call, or close to it,
chunks.st: at the crow of the rooster or adjacent to it,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says "gever" may also mean a man who called out to wake the Kohanim.

chunks.en: either before it or after it.
chunks.st: whether before it or after it,
chunks.stMore: as there was no insistence on a precise time.

chunks.en: On Yom Kippur, from midnight,
chunks.st: And on Yom Kippur they would remove the ashes earlier, from midnight onward.

chunks.en: and on the Yamim Tovim, from the end of the first watch.
chunks.st: And on the Festivals, the ashes were removed even earlier, at the end of the first watch.

words.note: The night was split into watches, like shifts of guards.

chunks.en: And the rooster's call would not come
chunks.st: And the call of the rooster would not arrive on Festivals

chunks.en: before the courtyard was full of Jews.
chunks.explain: So many people came with korbanos that the Kohanim started early.
chunks.st: until the Temple courtyard was full with the Jewish people who vowed to bring offerings and would fulfill their obligations on the Festivals.
chunks.stMore: Those offerings were sacrificed immediately following the daily offering.

words.note: The azarah, the big courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.summary: At first, any Kohen who wanted could clear the ashes from the mizbeach. If many wanted to, they raced up the ramp, and if two tied, they made a lottery by counting fingers.

chunks.en: At first, whoever wants
chunks.st: Initially, the practice among the priests was that whoever wishes to remove

chunks.en: to clear the ashes of the mizbeach, clears them.
chunks.st: the ashes from the altar removes them.

chunks.en: And when there are many Kohanim who want to,
chunks.st: And when there are many priests who wish to perform that task,
chunks.stMore: the privilege to do so is determined by a race:

chunks.en: they run and go up the ramp,
chunks.st: The priests run and ascend on the ramp leading to the top of the altar.

words.note: The sloping walkway leading up to the mizbeach.

chunks.en: and whoever gets ahead of his friend
chunks.st: Any priest who precedes another

chunks.en: within four amos of the top wins.
chunks.st: and reaches within four cubits of the top of the altar first is privileged to remove the ashes.

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm, from elbow to fingertips.

chunks.en: And if the two of them were even,
chunks.st: And if both of them were equal and neither preceded the other,

chunks.en: the one in charge says to them, "Put out your fingers."
chunks.explain: He counted the fingers to pick a Kohen, like a counting game.
chunks.st: the appointed priest says to all the priests: Extend your fingers,
chunks.stMore: and a lottery was performed, as will be explained.

chunks.en: And how many fingers do they put out?
chunks.st: And what fingers do they extend for the lottery?

chunks.en: One or two.
chunks.st: They may extend one or two fingers,

chunks.en: And they do not put out a thumb in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.explain: A thumb could look like another person's finger and spoil the count.
chunks.st: and the priests do not extend a thumb in the Temple.
chunks.stMore: The reason is that the lottery was conducted by the appointee choosing a number and counting the extended fingers of the priests standing in a circle. As the count progressed, a priest could calculate and manipulate the result in his favor by surreptitiously extending his thumb and an additional finger. Since there is separation between the thumb and the forefinger it could appear as though they belonged to two different priests, skewing the results of the lottery.

mishnayos.summary: Once two Kohanim raced up the ramp, one pushed the other, and he broke his leg. So the beis din made a rule that the ashes are cleared only by a lottery. There were four lotteries each day.

chunks.en: Once it happened that the two of them were even
chunks.st: Initially, that was the procedure; however, an incident occurred where both of them were equal as they were

chunks.en: as they ran and went up the ramp,
chunks.st: running and ascending on the ramp,

chunks.en: and one of them pushed his friend,
chunks.st: and one of them shoved another

chunks.en: and he fell and his leg broke.
chunks.st: and he fell and his leg was broken.

chunks.en: And when the beis din saw
chunks.st: And once the court saw that people

chunks.en: that they were coming to danger,
chunks.st: were coming to potential danger,

chunks.en: they made a rule that they would not clear
chunks.st: they instituted that priests would remove ashes from

chunks.en: the mizbeach except by a lottery.
chunks.st: the altar only by means of a lottery.

chunks.en: There were four lotteries there,
chunks.st: There were four lotteries there, in the Temple, on a daily basis to determine the priests privileged to perform the various services,

chunks.en: and this is the first lottery.
chunks.st: and this, determining which priest would remove the ashes, was the first lottery.

mishnayos.summary: The second lottery chose thirteen Kohanim: who would shecht the korban tamid, sprinkle its blood, clean the inside mizbeach and the Menorah, and carry the parts of the korban up the ramp.

chunks.en: The second lottery:
chunks.st: The second lottery conducted daily among the priests determines the following:

chunks.en: who shechts the korban,
chunks.st: Who slaughters the daily morning offering,

chunks.en: who sprinkles its blood,
chunks.st: who sprinkles its blood,

chunks.en: and who cleans the ashes from the inside mizbeach,
chunks.st: who removes the ashes from the inner altar,

words.note: The golden mizbeach inside the Heichal, where ketores was burned.

chunks.en: and who cleans the ashes from the Menorah,
chunks.st: and who removes the ashes and burnt wicks from the candelabrum,

chunks.en: and who carries the parts of the korban up to the ramp:
chunks.st: and who takes the limbs of the daily offering up to the ramp to be burned later.
chunks.stMore: This is how the limbs were divided before taking them up to the altar:

chunks.en: the head and the leg,
chunks.st: The head and the right leg were carried by one priest,

chunks.en: and the two front legs,
chunks.st: and the two forelegs were carried by a second priest.

words.note: Here it means the two front legs of the animal.

chunks.en: the tail and the other leg,
chunks.st: The tail, including the lower vertebrae of the spinal column and the fat tail, and the left leg were carried by a third priest.

chunks.en: the chest and the throat,
chunks.st: And the breast and the throat and some of the inner organs attached to it were carried by a fourth priest.

chunks.en: and the two sides,
chunks.st: And the two flanks were taken by a fifth priest,

chunks.en: and the insides, and the fine flour,
chunks.st: and the intestines by a sixth priest. And the fine flour of the meal-offering accompanying the daily offering was carried by a seventh priest.

words.note: Flour for the korban minchah that comes with the tamid.

chunks.en: and the griddle-cakes, and the wine.
chunks.st: And the High Priest’s daily griddle-cake offering was carried by an eighth priest, and the wine for libation was carried by a ninth priest.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol's daily minchah, cooked on a flat pan.
Wine poured on the mizbeach with the korban.

chunks.en: Thirteen Kohanim won in it.
chunks.st: Altogether thirteen priests prevailed in this lottery:
chunks.stMore: Nine priests who carried the daily offering and its accompanying elements, and four who performed the slaughter, sprinkling, and removal of ashes from the inner altar and the candelabrum.

chunks.he: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
chunks.en: Ben Azzai said before Rabbi Akiva
chunks.st: Ben Azzai said before Rabbi Akiva

chunks.en: in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: "It was brought in the way it walks."
chunks.explain: The parts went up in the order of the animal's body when it walks.
chunks.st: That was not the sequence of taking the limbs up to the ramp; rather, the order in which it was sacrificed was according to the way it walks when alive,
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.

mishnayos.summary: The third lottery was only for Kohanim who had never burned the ketores. The fourth lottery, open to all, chose who would carry the parts from the ramp up onto the mizbeach.

chunks.en: The third lottery:
chunks.st: Before the third lottery, the appointee declared:

chunks.en: "New ones for the ketores, come and make the lottery!"
chunks.explain: Only Kohanim who never burned the ketores could join.
chunks.st: Let only those priests who are new to offering the incense come and participate in the lottery for the incense.

chunks.en: And the fourth: new ones together with old ones,
chunks.st: The fourth lottery was open to those new to the service along with those old hands who had already performed it,to determine

chunks.he: מִי מַעֲלֶה אֵבָרִים מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ:
chunks.en: who carries the parts from the ramp up to the mizbeach.
chunks.st: who would take the limbs up from the ramp, where they had been placed earlier, to the altar.

chunks.en: The korban tamid is brought by nine Kohanim,
chunks.st: The daily offering is sacrificed and its limbs are carried by nine priests,
chunks.stMore: as mentioned in a previous mishna. These nine carry the limbs and the accompanying libations and meal-offerings.

words.note: The korban tamid is the daily korban, brought every morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: by ten, by eleven, by twelve,
chunks.st: Occasionally, the service is performed by ten priests, occasionally by eleven, and sometimes by twelve priests;

chunks.en: no fewer and no more.
chunks.st: no fewer than nine and no more than twelve.

chunks.en: How so? The tamid itself, by nine.
chunks.st: How so? The daily offering itself is sacrificed by nine priests, as explained earlier.

chunks.he: בֶּחָג, בְּיַד אֶחָד צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל מַיִם,
chunks.en: On Sukkos, one more holds a jug of water in his hand,
chunks.st: On the festival of Sukkot a priest in whose hand is a jug of water for the water libation is added,

words.note: Here it means the Yom Tov of Sukkos.
On Sukkos water was poured on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: so here there are ten.
chunks.st: and there are ten priests.

chunks.en: In the afternoon, by eleven:
chunks.st: In the daily afternoon offering, eleven priests participate in the service.

words.note: Bein ha'arbayim is the afternoon.

chunks.en: the tamid itself by nine,
chunks.st: How so? The daily offering itself is sacrificed by nine,

chunks.en: and two hold two logs of wood in their hands.

chunks.stMore: The mitzva of placing the two logs in the morning was assigned in the first lottery, as the Gemara explained earlier.

chunks.en: And on Shabbos, by eleven:
chunks.st: On Shabbat, eleven priests participate.

chunks.en: the tamid itself by nine,
chunks.st: How so? The daily morning offering itself is performed by nine,

chunks.en: and two hold in their hands
chunks.st: and there are an additional two priests in whose hands are

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי בְזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
chunks.en: two cups of levonah for the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: two vessels of frankincense that accompany the shewbread.
chunks.stMore: This frankincense is burned on Shabbat.

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice, frankincense.
The lechem hapanim are the twelve loaves on the Shulchan, changed every Shabbos.

chunks.en: And on a Shabbos during Sukkos,
chunks.st: And on Shabbat that occurs within the festival of Sukkot

chunks.en: one more holds a jug of water.
chunks.explain: That makes twelve Kohanim.
chunks.st: there is an additional priest in whose hand is a jug of water for the water libation, for a total of twelve priests.

mishnayos.summary: A ram brought as a korban olah is carried up by eleven Kohanim.

chunks.en: A ram is brought by eleven Kohanim:
chunks.st: A ram that is brought for a communal burnt-offering is sacrificed by eleven priests.

chunks.en: the meat by five,
chunks.st: The flesh on the various limbs is taken by five priests, as in the case of the sheep of the daily offering.

chunks.en: the insides, the fine flour and the wine by two each.
chunks.explain: A ram's flour and wine are bigger than a sheep's.
chunks.st: The intestines, and the fine flour of the meal-offering, and the wine of the libation are carried by two priests each,
chunks.stMore: because the meal-offering and wine libation that accompany a ram are larger than those that accompany a sheep.

mishnayos.summary: A bull brought as a korban is carried up by twenty-four Kohanim. This is for korbanos of the whole community; one person's korban may be brought by one Kohen if he wants.

chunks.en: A bull is brought by twenty-four Kohanim:
chunks.st: A bull is sacrificed by twenty-four priests. How so?

chunks.en: the head and the leg:
chunks.st: The head and the right leg are sacrificed first,

chunks.en: the head by one,
chunks.st: but due to its size the head is carried by one priest

chunks.en: and the leg by two.
chunks.st: and the leg by two.

chunks.en: The tail and the other leg:
chunks.st: The tail and the left leg are carried as follows:

chunks.en: the tail by two,
chunks.st: The tail is sacrificed by two

chunks.en: and the leg by two.
chunks.st: and the leg by two.

chunks.en: The chest and the throat:
chunks.st: The breast and the neck are carried as follows:

chunks.en: the chest by one,
chunks.st: The breast is offered by one

chunks.en: and the throat by three.
chunks.st: and the neck by three priests.

chunks.en: The two front legs by two.
chunks.st: The two forelegs are carried by two priests,

chunks.en: The two sides by two.
chunks.st: and the two flanks are carried by two.

chunks.en: The insides, the fine flour and the wine by three each.
chunks.st: The intestines and the fine flour and the wine are carried by three each,
chunks.stMore: because the meal-offering and wine libation that accompany a bull are larger than those that accompany a ram.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said, that this is the sequence followed?

chunks.en: For korbanos of the community.
chunks.st: It is in the case of communal offerings.

chunks.en: But for one person's korban,
chunks.st: However, in the case of an individual offering brought to fulfill a vow or an obligation,

chunks.en: if a Kohen wants to bring it alone, he brings it.
chunks.st: if a single priest wishes to sacrifice it alone he may sacrifice it alone, or if he chooses he may include other priests in the service.

chunks.he: הֶפְשֵׁטָן וְנִתּוּחָן שֶׁל אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שָׁוִין:
chunks.en: The skinning and cutting up of both of these are the same.
chunks.st: With regard to the flaying and the cutting of both these, individual offerings, and those, communal offerings, they are equal,
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.

mishnayos.summary: Before the morning korban could be shechted, a Kohen went to look if it was already day. He called out "Barkai!" which means the sky is bright.

chunks.en: The one in charge said to them,
chunks.st: The appointed priest said to the other priests:

chunks.he: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה.
chunks.en: "Go out and see if the time for shechitah has come."
chunks.st: Go out and observe if it is day and the time for slaughter has arrived.

chunks.en: If it had come,
chunks.st: If the time has arrived,

chunks.en: the one who saw it says, "Barkai!"
chunks.explain: Barkai means "it is getting light."
chunks.st: the observer says: There is light [barkai].

chunks.en: Masisya ben Shmuel says,
chunks.st: Matya ben Shmuel says that the appointed priest phrased his question differently:

chunks.he: הֵאִיר פְּנֵי כָל הַמִּזְרָח עַד שֶׁבְּחֶבְרוֹן.
chunks.en: "Is the whole eastern sky lit up, all the way to Chevron?"
chunks.st: Is the entire eastern sky illuminated even to Hebron?

chunks.en: And he says, "Yes."
chunks.st: And the observer says: Yes.

mishnayos.summary: They checked so carefully because once the moonlight fooled them and they shechted the tamid too early. Then the Kohen Gadol was brought to toivel, because anyone who goes into the azarah to serve must toivel.

chunks.en: And why did they need this?
Because once the moonlight came up,
and they thought the east was lit up,
and they shechted the tamid,
and they had to take it out to be burned.
chunks.explain: A korban shechted before daytime is not kosher.

chunks.en: They brought the Kohen Gadol down to the place for toiveling.
This was the rule in the Beis HaMikdash:

chunks.he: כָּל הַמֵּסֵךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו טָעוּן טְבִילָה,
chunks.en: Anyone who "covers his feet" must toivel,
chunks.explain: "Covers his feet" is a polite way to say he went to the bathroom.

chunks.he: וְכָל הַמַּטִּיל מַיִם טָעוּן קִדּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלָיִם:
chunks.en: and anyone who passes water must wash his hands and feet.

mishnayos.summary: Nobody may go into the azarah to serve until he toivels. On Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol toivels five times and washes his hands and feet ten times.

chunks.en: No one goes into the azarah for the service,
chunks.st: A person does not enter the Temple courtyard for the Temple service,

words.note: The big courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: even if he is tahor,
chunks.st: even if he is pure,

chunks.en: until he toivels.
chunks.st: until he immerses.

chunks.en: Five tevilos and ten washings
chunks.st: Five immersions and ten sanctifications

words.note: A tevilah is dipping the whole body in a mikveh.
Washing the hands and feet from the kiyor.

chunks.he: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol toivels and washes on that day,
chunks.st: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies his hands and feet, respectively, on the day of Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: and all of them are in the holy area, on top of the Parvah room,
chunks.st: And all of these immersions and sanctifications take place in the sacred area, the Temple courtyard, on the roof of the Hall of Parva,

words.note: A room in the Beis HaMikdash with a mikveh on its roof.

chunks.en: except for this one only.
chunks.explain: The first tevilah may be done outside the azarah.
chunks.st: except for this first immersion alone.
chunks.stMore: As that immersion is not unique to Yom Kippur, it may be performed outside the courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol toivels behind a linen sheet, puts on his golden clothes, and does the regular morning service of the korban tamid.

chunks.en: They spread out a sheet of linen
chunks.st: They spread a sheet of fine linen

chunks.en: between him and the people.
chunks.st: between him and the people in the interest of modesty,
chunks.stMore: and then the High Priest immersed and sanctified his hands and feet.

chunks.en: He took off his clothes, went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: The High Priest removed the white garments that he was wearing, descended to the ritual bath, and immersed.

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: He ascended and dried himself with a towel.

chunks.en: They brought him the golden clothes,
chunks.st: Then they brought him the golden garments of the High Priest,

words.note: The Kohen Gadol's special eight garments, with gold in them.

chunks.en: and he put them on, and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: and he dressed in the garments, and he sanctified his hands and his feet.

chunks.en: They brought him the tamid.
chunks.st: They brought him the sheep for the daily morning offering,

chunks.he: קְרָצוֹ, וּמֵרַק אַחֵר שְׁחִיטָה עַל יָדוֹ.
chunks.en: He cut it, and another Kohen finished the shechitah for him.
chunks.st: which he slaughtered by cutting most of the way through the gullet and the windpipe. And a different priest completed the slaughter on his behalf
chunks.stMore: so that the High Priest could receive the blood in a vessel and proceed with the order of the Yom Kippur service.

chunks.en: He caught the blood and sprinkled it.
chunks.st: As soon as the slaughter was completed, the High Priest received the blood in a vessel and sprinkled it on the altar.

chunks.en: He went in to burn the morning ketores,
chunks.st: He entered the Sanctuary to burn the morning incense

chunks.en: and to clean the lamps,
chunks.st: and to remove the ashes from the lamps of the candelabrum;

chunks.en: and to bring the head and the parts,
chunks.st: and he left the Sanctuary and returned to the courtyard to sacrifice the head and the limbs of the sheep sacrificed for the daily offering

chunks.en: and the griddle-cakes and the wine.
chunks.st: and the High Priest’s daily griddle-cake offering, and the wine libation of the daily offering.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells when the ketores is burned in the morning and in the afternoon. If the Kohen Gadol is old or delicate, they warm the mikveh water for him.

chunks.en: The morning ketores was
chunks.st: The Mishna comments: The morning incense

chunks.en: brought between the blood and the parts.
chunks.st: was burned between the receiving and sprinkling of the blood and the burning of the limbs;

chunks.en: And the afternoon ketores,
chunks.st: and the afternoon incense was burned

chunks.en: between the parts and the nesachim.
chunks.st: between the taking of the limbs up to the altar and the pouring of the libations that accompanied the offering.

words.note: The wine poured on the mizbeach with a korban.

chunks.en: If the Kohen Gadol was
chunks.st: With regard to the immersion, if the High Priest was old and found it difficult to immerse in cold water,

chunks.en: old or delicate,
chunks.st: or if he was delicate [istenis],

chunks.he: מְחַמִּין לוֹ חַמִּין וּמְטִילִין לְתוֹךְ הַצּוֹנֵן,
chunks.en: they heat hot water for him and pour it into the cold mikveh,
chunks.st: they would heat hot water for him on Yom Kippur eve and place it into the cold water of the ritual bath

chunks.en: so that its coldness will go away.
chunks.st: in order to temper its chill so the High Priest could immerse without discomfort.

mishnayos.summary: For the second tevilah, they bring the Kohen Gadol to the Parvah room. He toivels, puts on the white clothes, and washes his hands and feet.

chunks.en: They brought him to the Parvah room,
chunks.st: They brought the High Priest to immerse a second time in the Hall of Parva,

chunks.en: and it was in the holy area.
chunks.st: which was in the sacred area, the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: They spread out a sheet of linen
chunks.st: They spread a sheet of fine linen

chunks.en: between him and the people.
chunks.st: between him and the people in the interest of modesty.

chunks.en: He washed his hands and his feet, and took off his clothes.
chunks.st: And he sanctified his hands and his feet and removed his garments.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says that this was the sequence:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he took off his clothes, then washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: He first removed his garments and then he sanctified his hands and his feet.

chunks.en: He went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: He descended and immersed a second time.

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: He ascended and dried himself.

chunks.en: They brought him the white clothes,
chunks.explain: On Yom Kippur the special service is done in plain white linen.
chunks.st: And they immediately brought him the white garments,

chunks.en: he put them on and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: in which he dressed, and he sanctified his hands and his feet.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol's white linen clothes for Yom Kippur were very expensive. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue how much they cost.

chunks.en: In the morning he would wear Pelusium linen
chunks.st: In the morning he would wear linen garments from the Egyptian city of Pelusium

words.note: Fine linen from the city of Pelusium in Mitzrayim.

chunks.en: worth twelve maneh.
chunks.st: worth twelve maneh, 1,200 dinars or zuz.
chunks.stMore: These garments were very expensive due to their high quality.

words.note: A maneh is one hundred zuz, a lot of money.

chunks.en: And in the afternoon, Indian linen
chunks.st: And in the afternoon he wore linen garments from India, which were slightly less expensive,

chunks.en: worth eight hundred zuz.
chunks.st: worth eight hundred zuz.

words.note: A zuz is a silver coin.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: In the morning he would wear
chunks.st: In the morning he would wear garments

chunks.en: clothes worth eighteen maneh,
chunks.st: worth eighteen maneh,

chunks.he: וּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
chunks.en: and in the afternoon, clothes worth twelve maneh.
chunks.st: and in the afternoon he would wear garments worth twelve maneh.

chunks.en: Altogether, thirty maneh.
chunks.st: In total, the clothes were worth thirty maneh.

chunks.en: These were paid for by the community.
chunks.st: These sums for the garments came from the community,

chunks.en: And if he wanted to add,
chunks.st: and if the High Priest wished to add money to purchase even finer garments,

chunks.en: he adds from his own money.
chunks.st: he would add funding of his own.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol leans his hands on his bull and does viduy for himself and his family, asking Hashem to forgive them. Everyone answers "Baruch shem kevod malchuso le'olam va'ed."

chunks.en: He comes to his bull,
chunks.st: The High Priest comes and stands next to his bull,

chunks.he: וּפָרוֹ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: and his bull was standing between the Ulam and the mizbeach,
chunks.st: and his bull was standing between the Entrance Hall and the altar

words.note: The big entrance hall in front of the Heichal.

chunks.en: its head to the south and its face to the west.
chunks.st: with its head facing to the south and its face to the west.

chunks.en: And the Kohen stands on the east, facing west,
chunks.st: And the priest stands to the east of the bull, and his face points to the west.

chunks.en: and leans his two hands on it and says viduy.
chunks.explain: Viduy means saying out loud the sins and being sorry for them.
chunks.st: And the priest places his two hands on the bull and confesses.

chunks.en: And this is what he would say:
chunks.st: And this is what he would say in his confession:

chunks.en: "Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.he: עָוִיתִי פָּשַׁעְתִּי חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי.
chunks.en: I have done wrong, I have rebelled, I have sinned before You, I and my family.
chunks.st: I have sinned, I have done wrong, and I have rebelled before You, I and my family.

chunks.en: Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.en: please forgive the sins, the rebellions and the wrongs
chunks.st: grant atonement, please, for the sins, and for the wrongs, and for the rebellions

chunks.he: שֶׁעָוִיתִי וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי וְשֶׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי,
chunks.en: that I did wrong, rebelled and sinned before You, I and my family,
chunks.st: that I have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You, I and my family,

chunks.en: as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant (Vayikra 16):
chunks.st: as it is written in the Torah of Moses your servant:

chunks.en: 'For on this day He will forgive you,
chunks.st: “For on this day atonement shall be made for you

chunks.he: לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ.
chunks.en: to make you clean from all your sins; before Hashem you will be clean.'"
chunks.st: to cleanse you of all your sins; you shall be clean before the Lord” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: And they answer after him,
chunks.explain: They answer each time they hear the Kohen Gadol say Hashem's real Name.
chunks.st: And the priests and the people who were in the courtyard respond after he recites the name of God:

chunks.he: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and all time.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol goes to the two goats for the goral, the lottery that picks which goat is for Hashem. The lots were made of gold by Ben Gamla, and people praised him.

chunks.en: He comes to the east side of the azarah,
chunks.st: The priest then came to the eastern side of the Temple courtyard, farthest from the Holy of Holies,

chunks.en: to the north of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: to the north of the altar.

chunks.he: הַסְּגָן מִימִינוֹ וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
chunks.en: the Segan on his right and the head of the family on his left.
chunks.st: The deputy was to his right, and the head of the patrilineal family belonging to the priestly watch that was assigned to serve in the Temple that week was to his left.

words.note: The Kohen who is second to the Kohen Gadol.
The head of the family of Kohanim who served that day.

chunks.en: And there are two goats there,
chunks.st: And they arranged two goats there,

chunks.he: וְקַלְפִּי הָיְתָה שָׁם וּבָהּ שְׁנֵי גוֹרָלוֹת.
chunks.en: and a box was there with two lots in it.
chunks.st: and there was a lottery receptacle there, and in it were two lots.

words.note: Two tags, one saying "for Hashem" and one saying "for Azazel."

chunks.en: They were made of boxwood,
chunks.st: These were originally made of boxwood,

words.note: A kind of wood.

chunks.en: and Ben Gamla made them of gold,
chunks.st: and the High Priest Yehoshua ben Gamla fashioned them of gold,

words.note: Yehoshua ben Gamla, a Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: and they would mention him for praise.
chunks.st: and the people would mention him favorably for what he did.
chunks.stMore: Since the mishna mentions an item designed to enhance the Temple service, it also lists other such items:

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists people who gave beautiful gifts to the Beis HaMikdash and are remembered for good: Ben Katin, King Munbaz, Queen Helene, and Nikanor.

chunks.he: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר,
chunks.en: Ben Katin made twelve spouts for the kiyor,
chunks.st: The High Priest ben Katin made twelve spigots for the basin
chunks.stMore: so that several priests could sanctify their hands and feet at once,

words.note: A Kohen Gadol.
The big copper basin the Kohanim washed their hands and feet from.

chunks.en: because it had only two.
chunks.st: as previously the basin had only two.

chunks.en: He also made a machine for the kiyor,
chunks.st: He also made a machine [mukheni] for sinking the basin into flowing water during the night

chunks.en: so that its water would not become unfit by staying overnight.
chunks.explain: The machine lowered the kiyor into the water below every night.
chunks.st: so that its water would not be disqualified by remaining overnight.
chunks.stMore: Had the water remained in the basin overnight, it would have been necessary to pour it out the following morning. By immersing the basin in flowing water, the water inside remained fit for use the next morning.

chunks.he: מֻנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה כָל יְדוֹת
chunks.en: King Munbaz made all the handles
chunks.st: King Munbaz would contribute the funds required to

chunks.he: הַכֵּלִים שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁל זָהָב.
chunks.en: of the Yom Kippur vessels out of gold.
chunks.st: make the handles of all the Yom Kippur vessels of gold.

chunks.en: Helene his mother made a lamp
chunks.st: Queen Helene, his mother, fashioned a

chunks.he: שֶׁל זָהָב עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל.
chunks.en: of gold over the doorway of the Heichal.
chunks.st: decorative gold chandelier above the entrance of the Sanctuary.

words.note: The holy building inside the azarah, where the Menorah stood.

chunks.he: וְאַף הִיא עָשְׂתָה טַבְלָא שֶׁל זָהָב
chunks.en: She also made a tablet of gold
chunks.st: She also fashioned a golden tablet [tavla]

chunks.en: with the Torah section of Sotah written on it.
chunks.st: on which the Torah portion relating to sota was written.
chunks.stMore: The tablet could be utilized to copy this Torah portion, so that a Torah scroll need not be taken out for that purpose.

words.note: A part of the Torah in Bamidbar 5.

chunks.en: For Nikanor, miracles happened to his doors,
chunks.explain: The doors of the Nikanor Gate were saved by miracles.
chunks.st: With regard to Nicanor, miracles were performed to his doors, the doors in the gate of the Temple named for him, the Gate of Nicanor.

chunks.en: and they would mention them for praise.
chunks.st: And the people would mention all of those whose contributions were listed favorably.

mishnayos.summary: These people are remembered badly, because they did not want to teach their special skills to others. Good people are remembered for a bracha, and the names of the wicked rot away.

chunks.en: And these are remembered for shame:
chunks.st: the mishna lists those who took action in the Temple and were mentioned unfavorably.

chunks.en: The family of Garmu did not want
chunks.st: The craftsmen of the House of Garmu did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach how to make the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: the secret of the preparation of the shewbread and sought to keep the secret within their family.

chunks.en: The family of Avtinas did not want
chunks.st: The craftsmen of the House of Avtinas did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach how to make the ketores.
chunks.st: the secret of the preparation of the incense.

chunks.en: Hugras ben Levi knew
chunks.st: Also, Hugras ben Levi knew

chunks.en: a special way of singing, and did not want to teach it.
chunks.st: a chapter in the art of music, as will be explained, and he did not want to teach it to others.

chunks.en: Ben Kamtzar did not want
chunks.st: And the scribe ben Kamtzar did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach his special way of writing.
chunks.explain: He could write a four-letter word all at once.
chunks.st: a special act of writing.
chunks.stMore: He was expert at writing all four letters of a four-letter name simultaneously.

chunks.en: About the first ones it says (Mishlei 10),
chunks.st: About the first ones, who were mentioned favorably, it is stated:

chunks.en: "The memory of a tzaddik is for a bracha."
chunks.st: “The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing” (Proverbs 10:7);

chunks.en: And about these it says (there),
chunks.st: and about these who were concerned only for themselves it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the name of the wicked will rot."
chunks.st: “But the name of the wicked shall rot” (Proverbs 10:7).

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos the mention in the mishna of people who took action in the Temple and were mentioned favorably,

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol draws two lots from a box: one says "for Hashem" and one says "for Azazel." He puts them on the two goats and says, "For Hashem, a chatas."

chunks.en: He shook the box and took out two lots.
chunks.st: The High Priest would mix the lots in the lottery receptacle used to hold them and draw the two lots from it, one in each hand.

chunks.en: On one was written "For Hashem,"
chunks.st: Upon one was written: For God.

chunks.en: and on the other was written "For Azazel."
chunks.st: And upon the other one was written: For Azazel.

words.note: The goat for Azazel was sent away to a steep cliff in the desert.

chunks.he: הַסְּגָן בִּימִינוֹ וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
chunks.en: The Segan was at his right and the head of the family at his left.
chunks.st: The deputy High Priest would stand to the High Priest’s right, and the head of the patrilineal family would stand to his left.

chunks.en: If the lot "for Hashem" came up in his right hand,
chunks.st: If the lot for the name of God came up in his right hand,

chunks.en: the Segan says to him,
chunks.st: the Deputy would say to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My master, High Priest,

chunks.en: raise your right hand."
chunks.st: raise your right hand so that all can see with which hand the lot for God was selected.

chunks.en: And if the lot "for Hashem" came up in his left hand,
chunks.st: And if the lot for the name of God came up in his left hand,

chunks.en: the head of the family says to him,
chunks.st: the head of the patrilineal family would say to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My master, High Priest,

chunks.en: raise your left hand."
chunks.st: raise your left hand.

chunks.en: He put the lots on the two goats and says,
chunks.st: Then he would place the two lots upon the two goats,
chunks.stMore: the lot that arose in his right hand on the goat standing to his right side and the lot in his left hand on the goat to his left.

chunks.en: "For Hashem, a chatas."
chunks.st: And upon placing the lot for God upon the appropriate goat, he would say: For God, as a sin-offering.

words.note: A korban brought to make up for a sin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he did not need to say "a chatas,"
chunks.st: He need not say: As a sin-offering.

chunks.en: only "For Hashem."
chunks.st: Rather, it is sufficient to say: For God.

chunks.en: And they answer after him,
chunks.st: And upon saying the name of God, the priests and the people respond after him:

chunks.he: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and all time.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol ties a red strip on the goat that will be sent away. Then he does viduy a second time on his bull, this time for himself, his family, and all the Kohanim.

chunks.he: קָשַׁר לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית בְּרֹאשׁ שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
chunks.en: He tied a strip of red wool on the head of the goat that is sent away,
chunks.st: The High Priest tied a strip of crimson wool upon the head of the scapegoat

words.note: A strip shaped like a tongue.

chunks.en: and stood it facing the place it is sent from,
chunks.st: and positioned the goat opposite the place from which it was dispatched,
chunks.stMore: i.e., near the gate through which it was taken;

chunks.en: and the one to be shechted facing the place of its shechitah.
chunks.st: and the same was done to the goat that was to be slaughtered, opposite the place of its slaughter.

words.en: and the one to be shechted

chunks.en: He comes to his bull a second time,
chunks.st: He comes and stands next to his bull a second time,

chunks.en: and leans his two hands on it and says viduy.
chunks.st: and places his two hands upon it, and confesses.

chunks.en: And this is what he would say:
chunks.st: And this is what he would say:

chunks.en: "Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please God,

chunks.he: עָוִיתִי פָּשַׁעְתִּי חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי
chunks.en: I have done wrong, I have rebelled, I have sinned before You, I and my family
chunks.st: I have sinned, I have done wrong, and I have rebelled before You, I and my family

chunks.en: and the sons of Aharon, Your holy people.
chunks.st: and the children of Aaron, your sacred people.

chunks.en: Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please God,

chunks.en: please forgive the sins, the rebellions and the wrongs
chunks.st: grant atonement, please, for the sins, and for the wrongs, and for the rebellions

chunks.he: שֶׁעָוִיתִי וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי וְשֶׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי
chunks.en: that I did wrong, rebelled and sinned before You, I and my family
chunks.st: that I have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You, I, and my family,

chunks.en: and the sons of Aharon, Your holy people,
chunks.st: and the children of Aaron, your sacred people,

chunks.en: as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant (Vayikra 16):
chunks.st: as it is written in the Torah of Moses, your servant:

chunks.en: 'For on this day He will forgive you,
chunks.st: “For on this day atonement shall be made for you

chunks.he: לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ.
chunks.en: to make you clean from all your sins; before Hashem you will be clean.'"
chunks.st: to cleanse you of all your sins; you shall be clean before the Lord” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: And they answer after him,
chunks.st: And they, the priests and the people in the Temple courtyard, respond after him upon hearing the name of God:

chunks.he: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and all time.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol shechts his bull and gives the blood to a Kohen to stir. Then he takes a pan of burning coals from the mizbeach for the ketores.

chunks.en: He shechted it and caught its blood in a bowl,
chunks.st: The High Priest would slaughter the bull and receive its blood in a bowl,

chunks.en: and gave it to someone who stirs it
chunks.st: and give it to the one who stirs it.

chunks.en: on the fourth row of stones in the Heichal,
chunks.st: The stirrer would stand on the fourth row of tiles in the Sanctuary and stir the blood

chunks.en: so that it will not get hard.
chunks.explain: Blood left still gets thick, and then it cannot be sprinkled.
chunks.st: lest it coagulate while the High Priest sacrificed the incense.

chunks.en: He took a fire-pan and went up to the top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: He would take a coal pan and ascend to the top of the altar

chunks.en: and moved the coals to this side and that side,
chunks.st: and clear the upper layer of coals to this side and to that side

chunks.en: and scoops up from the inner, burned-down coals,
chunks.st: and with the coal pan scoop up coals from among the inner, consumed coals.

chunks.he: וְיָרַד וְהִנִּיחָהּ עַל הָרֹבֶד הָרְבִיעִי שֶׁבָּעֲזָרָה:
chunks.en: and went down and put it on the fourth row in the azarah.
chunks.st: And he would then descend and place the coal pan with the coals on the fourth row of tiles in the Temple courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Kippur the fire-pan for the coals and the ketores were special: the pan was gold, lighter and with a longer handle, and the ketores was ground extra fine.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם הָיָה חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל כֶּסֶף
chunks.en: Every day he would scoop with a silver pan
chunks.st: On every other day, a priest would scoop up the coals with a coal pan made of silver

chunks.en: and pour it into a gold one,
chunks.st: and pour the coals from there into a coal pan of gold.

chunks.en: but today he scoops with a gold one,
chunks.st: But on this day, on Yom Kippur, the High Priest scoops up with a coal pan of gold,

chunks.en: and with it he would bring them in.
chunks.explain: He brings the coals into the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: and with that coal pan he would bring the coals into the Holy of Holies.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין
chunks.en: Every day he scoops with a pan of four kav
chunks.st: On every other day, a priest scoops up the coals with a coal pan of four kav

words.note: A kav is a measure of volume.

chunks.en: and pours into one of three kav,
chunks.st: and pours the coals into a coal pan of three kav.

chunks.en: but today he scoops with one of three kav,
chunks.st: But on this day, the High Priest scoops with one of three kav,

chunks.en: and with it he would bring them in.
chunks.st: and with it he would bring the coals into the Holy of Holies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says a variation of this distinction:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Every day he scoops with a pan of a se'ah
chunks.st: On every other day, a priest scoops up the coals with a coal pan of a se’a, which is six kav

words.note: A se'ah is six kav.

chunks.en: and pours into one of three kav,
chunks.st: and then pours the coals into a coal pan of three kav.

chunks.en: but today he scoops with one of three kav,
chunks.st: But on this day, the High Priest scoops with a coal pan of three kav,

chunks.en: and with it he would bring them in.
chunks.st: and with it he would bring the coals into the Holy of Holies.

chunks.en: Every day the pan was heavy,
chunks.st: On every other day, the coal pan was heavy.

chunks.en: but today it is light.
chunks.explain: So the Kohen Gadol will not get tired.
chunks.st: But on this day it was light, so as not to tire the High Priest.

chunks.en: Every day its handle was short,
chunks.st: On every other day, its handle was short,

chunks.en: but today it is long.
chunks.st: but on this day it was long so that he could also use his arm to support its weight.

chunks.en: Every day its gold was greenish,
chunks.st: On every other day, it was of greenish gold,

chunks.en: but today it is red.
chunks.st: but on this day it was of a red gold.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Menachem.
chunks.st: These are the statements of Rabbi Menaḥem.

chunks.en: Every day one brings half a maneh of ketores
chunks.st: On every other day, a priest sacrificed a peras, half a maneh, of incense

words.note: Half of a maneh, a weight.

chunks.en: in the morning and half a maneh in the afternoon,
chunks.st: in the morning, and a peras in the afternoon,

chunks.en: but today he adds a full handful.
chunks.st: but on this day the High Priest adds an additional handful of incense and burns it in the Holy of Holies.

chunks.en: Every day the ketores was fine,
chunks.st: On every other day, the incense was ground fine as prescribed by the Torah,

chunks.en: but today it is the finest of the fine.
chunks.st: but on this day it was superfine.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna comments on some of the contrasts between the service and protocols followed on Yom Kippur and those followed throughout the rest of the year:

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol goes up and down the middle of the ramp, and washes his hands and feet from a golden jug. Rabbi Yehuda says he always does so.

chunks.en: Every day the Kohanim go up on the east side
chunks.st: On every other day, priests ascend on the eastern side of the ramp

chunks.en: of the ramp and go down on its west side,
chunks.st: and descend on its western side,

chunks.en: but today the Kohen Gadol goes up in the middle
chunks.st: but on this day the High Priest ascends in the middle of the ramp

chunks.en: and goes down in the middle.
chunks.st: and descends in the middle.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: There was no difference in this regard. Even during the rest of the year,

chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol always goes up in the middle
chunks.explain: Because he is so important.
chunks.st: the High Priest always ascends in the middle of the ramp

chunks.en: and goes down in the middle.
chunks.st: and descends in the middle, due to his eminence.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
chunks.en: Every day the Kohen Gadol washes his hands and his feet
chunks.st: On every other day, the High Priest sanctifies his hands and his feet

chunks.en: from the kiyor,
chunks.st: from the laver like the other priests,

chunks.en: but today from the golden jug.
chunks.st: and on this day he sanctifies them from the golden flask, due to the eminence of the High Priest.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says there was no difference in this regard. Even during the rest of the year,

chunks.he: לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol always washes his hands and his feet
chunks.st: the High Priest always sanctifies his hands and his feet

chunks.en: from the golden jug.
chunks.st: from the golden flask.

mishnayos.summary: There were more piles of burning wood on the mizbeach on Yom Kippur than on other days. Three Tannaim argue how many.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבַּע מַעֲרָכוֹת,
chunks.en: Every day there were four piles of wood there,
chunks.st: On every other day there were four arrangements of wood there, upon the altar,

chunks.en: but today five.
chunks.st: but on this day there were five; this is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: every day three,
chunks.st: On every other day there were three,

chunks.en: and today four.
chunks.st: but on this day there were four.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: every day two,
chunks.st: On every other day there were two,

chunks.en: and today three.
chunks.st: but on this day there were three.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol takes a handful of ketores and a pan of coals and walks into the Kodesh HaKodashim. He puts the ketores on the coals, and the room fills with smoke. Then he comes out and says a short tefillah.

chunks.he: הוֹצִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה,
chunks.en: They brought out to him the spoon and the fire-pan,
chunks.st: They brought out the spoon and the coal pan to the High Priest so he may perform the service of the incense.

chunks.he: וְחָפַן מְלֹא חָפְנָיו וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ הַכַּף,
chunks.en: and he took his full handfuls and put them into the spoon,
chunks.st: He scoops his handfuls from the incense and places it into the spoon.

chunks.en: a big one according to his size,
chunks.explain: A Kohen Gadol with big hands takes more ketores.
chunks.st: The High Priest with large hands fills the spoon with incense in an amount corresponding to the large size of his hands,

chunks.en: and a small one according to his size,
chunks.st: and the High Priest with small hands fills the spoon with incense in an amount corresponding to the small size of his hands.

chunks.en: and this was its measure.
chunks.st: And this was the measure of the spoon, i.e., it was made to correspond to the size of his hands.

chunks.en: He took the fire-pan in his right hand
chunks.st: He took the coal pan in his right hand

chunks.en: and the spoon in his left hand.
chunks.st: and the spoon in his left hand.

chunks.en: He would walk through the Heichal,
chunks.st: The High Priest would then walk west through the Sanctuary

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְבֵין שְׁתֵּי הַפָּרֹכוֹת הַמַּבְדִּילוֹת
chunks.en: until he reaches between the two curtains that separate
chunks.st: until he reaches the area between the two curtains that separated

chunks.en: between the Kodesh and the Kodesh HaKodashim,
chunks.st: the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies, and

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim is the holiest room, where the Aron stood.

chunks.en: and between them was one amah.
chunks.st: the space between them was one cubit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.he: לֹא הָיְתָה שָׁם אֶלָּא פָרֹכֶת אַחַת בִּלְבָד,
chunks.en: there was only one curtain there,
chunks.st: There was only one curtain there,

chunks.en: as it says (Shemos 26),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the curtain will separate for you
chunks.st: “And the curtain shall divide for you

chunks.en: between the Kodesh and the Kodesh HaKodashim."
chunks.st: between the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies” (Exodus 26:33).

chunks.en: The outer one was hooked open on the south side,
chunks.st: The outer curtain between the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies was hooked [perufa] slightly open on the south side of the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: and the inner one on the north side.
chunks.st: and the inner curtain hooked slightly open on the north side of the Sanctuary,
chunks.stMore: and therefore the High Priest could not enter the Holy of Holies directly.

chunks.en: He walks between them,
chunks.st: Rather, he enters through the southern opening and walks between the curtains

chunks.en: until he reaches the north side.
chunks.st: until he reaches the opening to the north.

chunks.en: When he reached the north side,
chunks.st: When he reaches the opening to the north,

chunks.en: he turns his face to the south,
chunks.st: he enters the Holy of Holies through that opening, turns his face to the south,

chunks.en: he walks to his left along the curtain
chunks.st: and walks to his left along the curtain

chunks.en: until he reaches the Aron.
chunks.st: until he reaches the area before the Ark.

words.note: The Aron is the holy box that held the Luchos.

chunks.en: He reached the Aron.
chunks.st: When he reaches the Ark,

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַבַּדִּים.
chunks.en: He puts the fire-pan between the two poles.
chunks.st: he places the coal pan between the two staves.

words.note: The two long poles used to carry the Aron.

chunks.he: צָבַר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי גֶחָלִים,
chunks.en: He piled the ketores on top of the coals,
chunks.st: He piles the incense atop the coals,

chunks.en: and the whole room filled up with smoke.
chunks.st: and the whole chamber in its entirety would fill with smoke.

chunks.he: יָצָא וּבָא לוֹ בְדֶרֶךְ בֵּית כְּנִיסָתוֹ,
chunks.en: He came out the same way he went in,
chunks.st: He then exits and comes out the way that he entered.
chunks.stMore: He does not turn around but leaves the Holy of Holies walking while facing the Ark.

chunks.en: and says a short tefillah in the outer room,
chunks.st: And he recites a brief prayer in the outer chamber, in the Sanctuary.

chunks.en: and he would not make his tefillah long,
chunks.st: And he would not extend his prayer there

chunks.en: so as not to frighten the Jewish people.
chunks.explain: If he took long, people would worry something bad happened to him.
chunks.st: so as not to alarm the Jewish people,
chunks.stMore: who would otherwise conclude that something happened and that he died in the Holy of Holies.

mishnayos.summary: After the Aron was hidden away, there was a stone in the Kodesh HaKodashim called the Even Shesiyah. The Kohen Gadol put the ketores on it.

chunks.en: After the Aron was taken away,
chunks.st: After the Ark was taken into exile,

chunks.he: אֶבֶן הָיְתָה שָׁם מִימוֹת נְבִיאִים רִאשׁוֹנִים,
chunks.en: there was a stone there from the days of the first Nevi'im,
chunks.st: there was a rock in the Holy of Holies from the days of the early prophets,
chunks.stMore: David and Samuel, who laid the groundwork for construction of the Temple,

words.note: Prophets.

chunks.en: and it was called Shesiyah, the foundation stone.
chunks.st: and this stone was called the foundation rock.

chunks.en: three fingers higher than the ground,
chunks.st: It was three fingerbreadths higher than the ground,

chunks.en: and he would put the pan on it.
chunks.st: and the High Priest would place the incense on it.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol takes the bull's blood back into the Kodesh HaKodashim and sprinkles it, one time up and seven times down, counting carefully so he won't make a mistake.

chunks.en: He took the blood from the one
chunks.st: he took the blood of the bull sacrificed as a sin-offering from the one

chunks.en: who was stirring it,
chunks.st: who was stirring it, so it would not coagulate.

chunks.en: he went into the place where he went in before,
chunks.st: He entered into the place that he had previously entered, the Holy of Holies,

chunks.en: and stood in the place where he stood before,
chunks.st: and stood at the place where he had previously stood to offer the incense, between the staves.

chunks.he: וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה,
chunks.en: and sprinkled from it once upward and seven times downward,
chunks.st: And he sprinkled from the blood, one time upward and seven times downward.

chunks.en: and he did not try to sprinkle
chunks.st: And he would neither intend to sprinkle the blood

chunks.he: לֹא לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה, אֶלָּא כְמַצְלִיף.

chunks.explain: The drops landed in a line, one under the other.
chunks.st: upward nor to sprinkle it downward, but rather like one who whips, with the blood sprinkled in a single column, one drop below the other.

chunks.he: וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנֶה, אַחַת, אַחַת וְאַחַת,
chunks.en: And this is how he would count: "One, one and one,
chunks.st: And this is how he would count as he sprinkled, to avoid error: One; one and one;

chunks.he: אַחַת וּשְׁתַּיִם, אַחַת וְשָׁלשׁ, אַחַת וְאַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: one and two, one and three, one and four,
chunks.st: one and two; one and three; one and four;

chunks.he: אַחַת וְחָמֵשׁ, אַחַת וָשֵׁשׁ, אַחַת וָשֶׁבַע.
chunks.en: one and five, one and six, one and seven."

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol puts the mixed blood on the four corners of the golden mizbeach, going around it in order. Rabbi Eliezer says he stood in one place.

chunks.he: וְיָצָא אֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי יְיָ,
chunks.en: "And he will go out to the mizbeach that is before Hashem"
chunks.st: “And he shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord,
chunks.stMore: and make atonement for it; and he shall take of the blood of the bull, and of the blood of the goat, and place it upon the corners of the altar round about” (Leviticus 16:18).

chunks.en: this is the golden mizbeach.
chunks.st: This altar is the golden altar,
chunks.stMore: since the outer altar is not before the Lord in the Sanctuary.

chunks.en: He began putting blood on it, going downward.
chunks.st: He began to cleanse the altar, sprinkling the blood downward.

chunks.en: Where does he begin?
chunks.st: From where does he begin?

chunks.en: From the northeast corner,
chunks.st: He begins from the northeast corner,

chunks.en: then the northwest,
chunks.st: and proceeds to the northwest corner,

chunks.en: then the southwest,
chunks.st: and then to the southwest corner,

chunks.en: then the southeast.
chunks.st: and finally to the southeast corner.

chunks.en: The place where he begins with a chatas
chunks.st: A way to remember this is: At the place where he begins sprinkling the blood for a sin-offering sacrificed

chunks.en: on the outer mizbeach,
chunks.st: on the outer altar, the southeast corner,

chunks.he: מִשָּׁם הָיָה גוֹמֵר עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי.
chunks.en: that is where he would finish on the inner mizbeach.
chunks.st: there he finishes sprinkling the blood on the inner altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he would stand in his place and put on the blood.
chunks.explain: The golden mizbeach was small, so he could reach every corner.
chunks.st: The priest would not circle the altar; rather, he stood in one place and sprinkled the blood from there.
chunks.stMore: Since the altar was only one square cubit, he could sprinkle the blood on all four corners without moving.

chunks.he: וְעַל כֻּלָּן הָיָה נוֹתֵן מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה,
chunks.en: And on all of them he would put it from below going up,
chunks.st: And on all the corners he would present the blood from below upward,

chunks.en: except for the one right in front of him,
chunks.st: except for that corner that was directly before him,

chunks.en: where he would put it from above going down.
chunks.st: on which he would present the blood from above downward.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol sprinkles blood seven times on the top of the golden mizbeach and pours what is left on the base of the outer mizbeach. The leftover blood flows out to Nachal Kidron.

chunks.he: הִזָּה עַל טָהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים,
chunks.en: He sprinkled on the clean top of the mizbeach seven times,
chunks.explain: He first moved the ashes aside so the gold showed.
chunks.st: He sprinkled blood on the pure gold of the altar seven times after clearing away the ashes.

chunks.en: and the rest of the blood he would pour
chunks.st: And he would pour the remainder of the blood

chunks.he: עַל יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן,
chunks.en: on the western base of the outer mizbeach.
chunks.st: on the western base of the outer altar.

words.note: The bottom ledge around the mizbeach.

chunks.en: And the blood of the outer mizbeach, he would pour
chunks.st: On a related topic, the mishna teaches that he would pour the remaining blood of an offering, after it was sprinkled, on the outer altar,

chunks.en: on the southern base.
chunks.st: on its southern base.

chunks.en: These and these mix together in the canal
chunks.st: These remainders of blood from the outer altar and those remainders of blood from the inner altar are mixed in the canal beneath the altar
