chunks.en: and flow out to Nachal Kidron,
chunks.st: and flow out with the water used to rinse the area to the Kidron River.

words.note: A valley next to Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and are sold to gardeners to help plants grow,
chunks.st: This water was sold to gardeners for use as fertilizer.
chunks.stMore: The gardeners paid for this water and thereby redeemed it from its sanctity.

chunks.en: and one who uses it without paying does me'ilah.
chunks.explain: Me'ilah means using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: Failure to do so would render them guilty of misuse of consecrated property.

mishnayos.summary: The Yom Kippur service must be done in the right order. If the blood spills in the middle, the Kohen Gadol brings new blood and starts that part again.

chunks.he: כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאָמוּר עַל הַסֵּדֶר,
chunks.en: All the Yom Kippur service that is said in order:
chunks.st: Each action performed in the context of the service of Yom Kippur stated in the mishna, as in the Torah, is listed in order.

chunks.en: if he did one thing before another,
chunks.st: If the High Priest performed one of the actions before another,

chunks.en: he did nothing.
chunks.st: he has done nothing.

chunks.en: If he put the goat's blood before the bull's blood,
chunks.st: If he performed the sprinkling of the blood of the goat before the sprinkling of the blood of the bull,

chunks.en: he must go back and sprinkle from the goat's blood
chunks.st: he must repeat the action and sprinkle the blood of the goat

chunks.en: after the bull's blood.
chunks.st: after sprinkling the blood of the bull, so that the actions are performed in the proper order.

chunks.he: וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָמַר אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת
chunks.en: And if before he finished the sprinklings
chunks.st: And if the blood spills before he completed the presentations

chunks.en: inside, the blood spilled,
chunks.st: that were sprinkled inside the Holy of Holies,

chunks.he: יָבִיא דָם אַחֵר וְיַחֲזֹר וְיַזֶּה בַתְּחִלָּה בִּפְנִים.
chunks.en: he brings other blood and starts again inside from the beginning.
chunks.st: he must slaughter another bull or goat, and bring other blood, and then repeat all the services from the beginning inside the Holy of Holies.

chunks.en: And the same in the Heichal,
chunks.st: And similarly, if the blood spills before he finishes the presentations in the Sanctuary, he must begin the service in the Sanctuary from the beginning,

chunks.en: and the same on the golden mizbeach,
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to the sprinkling of blood on the golden altar.

chunks.en: because each one is a kapparah by itself.
chunks.st: Since they are each acts of atonement in and of themselves,
chunks.stMore: there is no need to repeat the service of the entire day from the beginning. Rather, he need only repeat the specific element that he failed to complete.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:

chunks.en: from the place where he stopped,
chunks.st: From the place that he interrupted that particular service, when the blood spilled,

chunks.en: from there he begins.
chunks.st: there he resumes performance of that service.
chunks.stMore: In their opinion, each individual sprinkling in each of these services is an act in and of itself, and there is no need to repeat what he has already done.

mishnayos.summary: The two goats of Yom Kippur should look the same and be bought together. If one of them dies, this mishnah teaches what to do.

chunks.en: The two goats of Yom Kippur:
chunks.st: The mitzva of the two Yom Kippur goats, the goat sacrificed to God and the goat sent to Azazel that are brought as a pair, is as follows, ab initio:

chunks.en: the mitzvah is that both of them should be the same in looks,
chunks.st: That they will both be identical in appearance, i.e., color,

chunks.en: and in height, and in price, and be bought together.
chunks.st: and in height, and in monetary value, and their acquisition must be as one, i.e., they must be purchased together.

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן שָׁוִין, כְּשֵׁרִין.
chunks.en: And even if they are not the same, they are kosher.
chunks.st: And even if they are not identical, nevertheless, they are valid.

chunks.he: לָקַח אֶחָד הַיּוֹם וְאֶחָד לְמָחָר, כְּשֵׁרִין.
chunks.en: If he bought one today and one tomorrow, they are kosher.
chunks.st: And similarly, if he acquired one today and one tomorrow, they are valid.

chunks.en: If one of them died,
chunks.st: If one of the goats died,

chunks.en: if it died before he drew the lots,
chunks.st: if it died before the High Priest drew the lots,

chunks.en: he takes a partner for the second one.
chunks.st: he immediately takes a counterpart for the second, since neither has yet been designated.

chunks.en: And if it died after he drew the lots,
chunks.st: And if it died after the High Priest drew the lots,

chunks.he: יָבִיא זוּג אַחֵר וְיַגְרִיל עֲלֵיהֶם בַּתְּחִלָּה,
chunks.en: he brings another pair and draws lots on them from the start,
chunks.st: he brings another pair of goats and draws lots over them from the start.

chunks.en: and he says, "If the one for Hashem died,
chunks.st: After that lottery he utters a stipulation: If the one to be sacrificed to God died,

chunks.en: this one, that the lot for Hashem
chunks.st: that goat upon which the lot for God was drawn in the second lottery

chunks.en: came up on, will stand in its place.
chunks.st: shall stand in its stead;

chunks.en: And if the one for Azazel died,
chunks.st: and if the one to be sent to Azazel died,

chunks.en: this one, that the lot for Azazel
chunks.st: that goat upon which the lot for Azazel was drawn

chunks.en: came up on, will stand in its place."
chunks.st: shall stand in its stead.

chunks.en: And the second one grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.explain: A mum is a blemish that makes an animal unfit for a korban.
chunks.st: And the second, superfluous goat, i.e., in the case where a new pair of goats was brought, should graze until it becomes unfit,

chunks.en: and it is sold, and its money goes to a gift korban,
chunks.st: at which point it will be sold, and the money received from its sale will go toward the purchase of a public gift-offering.
chunks.stMore: Although for individual sin-offerings in similar circumstances there is no remedy and it is left to die, that is not the case here,

chunks.en: because a chatas of the community is not left to die.
chunks.st: as a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, it should be left to die.
chunks.st: On the other hand, Rabbi Yehuda says: In this it should be left to die.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehuda said more:
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: If the blood spilled,
chunks.st: If the blood of the goat sacrificed to God spilled before it was sprinkled,

chunks.en: the goat to be sent away is left to die.
chunks.st: the scapegoat is left to die.

chunks.en: If the goat to be sent away died,
chunks.st: Similarly, if the scapegoat dies,

chunks.en: the blood is spilled out.
chunks.explain: Then they bring two new goats and start over.
chunks.st: the blood of the goat sacrificed to God should be spilled, and two other goats are brought and lots are drawn.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol leans his hands on the goat for Azazel and does viduy for all of the Jewish people. When the people hear Hashem's holy Name, they bow down and answer "Baruch shem."

chunks.en: He comes to the goat that is sent away,
chunks.st: The Yom Kippur service continues: The High Priest comes over to the scapegoat,

chunks.en: and leans his two hands on it and says viduy.
chunks.st: places both his hands upon it, and confesses.

chunks.en: And this is what he would say:
chunks.st: And he would say as follows:

chunks.en: "Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.he: עָווּ פָּשְׁעוּ חָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל.
chunks.en: Your people, the house of Yisrael, have done wrong, rebelled and sinned before You.
chunks.st: Your people, the house of Israel, have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You.

chunks.en: Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.en: please forgive the sins, the rebellions and the wrongs
chunks.st: grant atonement, please, for the sins, and for the wrongs, and for the rebellions

chunks.he: שֶׁעָווּ וְשֶׁפָּשְׁעוּ וְשֶׁחָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: that Your people, the house of Yisrael, did wrong, rebelled and sinned before You,
chunks.st: that they have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You, Your people, the house of Israel,

chunks.he: כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַת משֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ לֵאמֹר (ויקרא טז),
chunks.en: as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant (Vayikra 16):
chunks.st: as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant, saying:

chunks.en: 'For on this day He will forgive you,
chunks.st: “For on this day atonement shall be made for you

chunks.he: לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ.
chunks.en: to make you clean from all your sins; before Hashem you will be clean.'"
chunks.st: to cleanse you of all your sins; before the Lord you shall be purified” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: And the Kohanim and the people standing in the azarah,
chunks.st: And the priests and the people standing in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: when they would hear the special Name of Hashem
chunks.st: when they would hear the Explicit Name

words.note: Hashem's holy Name, said only by the Kohen Gadol in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: coming out of the mouth of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: emerging from the mouth of the High Priest, when the High Priest did not use one of the substitute names for God,

chunks.he: הָיוּ כּוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְנוֹפְלִים עַל פְּנֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: they would bow down on their knees and fall on their faces,
chunks.st: they would kneel and prostrate themselves and fall on their faces,

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים, בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: and say, "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: and say: Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.

mishnayos.summary: The goat for Azazel is given to a man who leads it out to the desert. Anyone may do it, but the Kohanim Gedolim made a rule to give it only to a Kohen.

chunks.en: He gave it to the one who was leading it.
chunks.st: passed the goat to the one who was to lead it to the wilderness.

chunks.en: Anyone is allowed to lead it,
chunks.st: According to the halakha, everyone is eligible to lead it,

chunks.en: but the Kohanim Gedolim made it a fixed rule
chunks.st: but the High Priests established a fixed custom

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוֹלִיכוֹ.
chunks.en: and did not let a Yisrael lead it.
chunks.explain: A Yisrael is a Jew who is not a Kohen or a Levi.
chunks.st: and did not allow an Israelite to lead it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,

chunks.st: or who drinks a cheekful of liquid on Yom Kippur is liable to receive the punishment of karet for failing to fulfill the mitzva to afflict oneself on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: All foods add up together to the size of a date.
chunks.st: All foods that one eats join together to constitute a date-bulk;

words.en: to the size of a date

chunks.en: All drinks add up together to a full cheekful.
chunks.st: and all liquids that one drinks join together to constitute a cheekful.

chunks.en: One who eats and drinks,
chunks.st: However, if one eats and drinks, the food and beverage

chunks.en: they do not add up together.
chunks.st: do not join together to constitute a measure that determines liability, as each is measured separately.

mishnayos.summary: If someone forgot it was Yom Kippur and ate and drank, he brings one korban chatas. If he also did melachah, he brings two. Eating things that are not food does not count.

chunks.en: If he ate and drank while he forgot one time,
chunks.st: If one ate and drank unwittingly within one lapse of awareness, e.g., he forgot that it is Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: he only has to bring one chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one sin-offering.

chunks.en: If he ate and did melachah,
chunks.st: However, if he ate and performed labor unwittingly,

words.note: Work that is forbidden on Shabbos and Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: he has to bring two chataos.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring two sin-offerings, as by doing so he violated two separate prohibitions.

chunks.en: If he ate foods that are not fit for eating,
chunks.st: If he ate foods that are not fit for eating,

chunks.en: or drank drinks that are not fit for drinking,
chunks.st: or drank liquids that are not fit for drinking,

chunks.en: or drank fish brine or fish pickle juice, he is free.
chunks.explain: People do not normally eat or drink these.
chunks.st: or drank fish brine or the briny liquid in which fish are pickled, he is exempt, as that is not the typical manner of eating or drinking.

mishnayos.summary: Small children do not have to fast on Yom Kippur, but a year or two before their bar or bas mitzvah we train them to fast a little, so they get used to mitzvos.

chunks.he: הַתִּינוֹקוֹת, אֵין מְעַנִּין אוֹתָן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
chunks.en: Little children: we do not make them fast on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: With regard to the children, one does not afflict them by withholding food on Yom Kippur;

chunks.en: but we train them
chunks.st: however, one trains them

chunks.en: one year before and two years before,
chunks.explain: Before they become bar or bas mitzvah.
chunks.st: one year before or two years before they reach majority, by means of a partial fast lasting several hours,

chunks.en: so that they will be used to the mitzvos.
chunks.st: so that they will be accustomed to fulfill mitzvot.

mishnayos.summary: A pregnant woman who smells food and needs it is fed. A sick person is fed if doctors say he needs it, or if he himself says so.

chunks.en: A pregnant woman who smelled food,
chunks.st: With regard to a pregnant woman who smelled food and was overcome by a craving to eat it,

chunks.en: we feed her until she feels better.
chunks.st: one feeds her until she recovers,
chunks.stMore: as failure to do so could lead to a life-threatening situation.

chunks.he: חוֹלֶה מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי בְקִיאִין.
chunks.en: A sick person, we feed him if experts say so.
chunks.st: If a person is ill and requires food due to potential danger, one feeds him according to the advice of medical experts who determine that he indeed requires food.

chunks.en: And if there are no experts there,
chunks.st: And if there are no experts there,

chunks.en: we feed him if he himself says so,
chunks.st: one feeds him according to his own instructions,

chunks.en: until he says, "Enough."
chunks.st: until he says that he has eaten enough and needs no more.

mishnayos.summary: A person who is very sick from hunger may be fed even non-kosher food. The mishnah also teaches that when a life may be in danger, we do whatever is needed, even on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Someone who is seized by bulmos,
chunks.explain: Bulmos is a dangerous sickness of terrible hunger.
chunks.st: In the case of one who is seized with the life-threatening illness bulmos, causing him unbearable hunger pangs and impaired vision,

chunks.en: we feed him even food that is tamei,
chunks.st: one may feed him even impure foods on Yom Kippur or any other day

chunks.en: until his eyes light up.
chunks.explain: When he can see well again, he is getting better.
chunks.st: until his eyes recover, as the return of his sight indicates that he is recovering.

chunks.en: Someone who was bitten by a crazy dog,
chunks.st: In the case of one whom a mad dog bit,

chunks.he: אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲצַר כָּבֵד שֶׁלוֹ,
chunks.en: we do not feed him from the lobe of its liver,
chunks.explain: Some people thought this would cure him, but the Sages said it does not work.
chunks.st: one may not feed him from the lobe of the dog’s liver.
chunks.stMore: This was thought to be a remedy for the bite, but the Rabbis deem it ineffective.

chunks.en: and Rabbi Masya ben Charash allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash permits feeding it to him, as he deems it effective.

chunks.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶן חָרָשׁ,
chunks.en: And Rabbi Masya ben Charash said more:
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash said:

chunks.en: Someone whose throat hurts,
chunks.st: With regard to one who suffers pain in his throat,

chunks.he: מַטִּילִין לוֹ סַם בְּתוֹךְ פִּיו בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: we put medicine into his mouth on Shabbos,
chunks.st: one may place medicine inside his mouth on Shabbat, although administering a remedy is prohibited on Shabbat.

chunks.en: because maybe his life is in danger,
chunks.st: This is because there is uncertainty whether or not it is a life-threatening situation for him, as it is difficult to ascertain the severity of internal pain.

chunks.he: וְכָל סְפֵק נְפָשׁוֹת דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת:
chunks.en: and anything where a life may be in danger pushes aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: And a case of uncertainty concerning a life-threatening situation overrides Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: If a building fell on someone, and we are not sure if he is there or if he is alive, we dig him out even on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Someone that a fallen building fell on,
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to one upon whom a rockslide fell,

chunks.he: סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם,
chunks.en: maybe he is there, maybe he is not there,
chunks.st: and there is uncertainty whether he is there under the debris or whether he is not there;

chunks.en: maybe alive, maybe not alive,
chunks.st: and there is uncertainty whether he is still alive or whether he is dead;

chunks.en: maybe a non-Jew, maybe a Jew,
chunks.st: and there is uncertainty whether the person under the debris is a gentile or whether he is a Jew,

chunks.en: we clear the pile off him.
chunks.st: one clears the pile from atop him.
chunks.stMore: One may perform any action necessary to rescue him from beneath the debris.

chunks.en: If they found him alive,
chunks.st: If they found him alive after beginning to clear the debris,

chunks.en: they keep clearing for him.
chunks.st: they continue to clear the pile until they can extricate him.

chunks.en: And if he is not alive, they leave him.
chunks.explain: We may not break Shabbos only for someone who is no longer alive.
chunks.st: And if they found him dead, they should leave him, since one may not desecrate Shabbat to preserve the dignity of the dead.

mishnayos.summary: Korbanos, Yom Kippur and teshuvah bring forgiveness. Teshuvah forgives small sins, and for big sins it holds them back until Yom Kippur forgives.

chunks.en: A chatas and a sure asham bring forgiveness.
chunks.st: A sin-offering, which atones for unwitting performance of transgressions punishable by karet, and a definite guilt-offering, which is brought for robbery and misuse of consecrated items, atone for those sins.

words.note: An asham is a korban brought for certain sins, like stealing.

chunks.he: מִיתָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפְּרִין עִם הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
chunks.en: Death and Yom Kippur bring forgiveness together with teshuvah.
chunks.st: Death and Yom Kippur atone for sins when accompanied by repentance.

words.note: Teshuvah means being sorry for a sin and coming back to Hashem.

chunks.en: Teshuvah forgives light sins,
chunks.st: Repentance itself atones for minor transgressions,

chunks.en: both for a mitzvas aseh and for a lo sa'aseh.
chunks.explain: A mitzvah to do something, or a mitzvah not to do something.
chunks.st: for both positive mitzvot and negative mitzvot.

chunks.en: And for the serious sins, it holds them back
chunks.st: And repentance places punishment for severe transgressions in abeyance

chunks.en: until Yom Kippur comes and forgives.
chunks.st: until Yom Kippur comes and completely atones for the transgression.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who plans to sin and do teshuvah later will not be helped to do teshuvah. Yom Kippur forgives sins against Hashem, but sins against another person are forgiven only after he makes up with that person. Hashem makes the Jewish people pure.

chunks.en: One who says, "I will sin and then do teshuvah,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: I will sin and then I will repent,

chunks.en: I will sin and then do teshuvah,"
chunks.st: I will sin and I will repent,

chunks.en: is not given the chance to do teshuvah.
chunks.st: Heaven does not provide him the opportunity to repent,
chunks.stMore: and he will remain a sinner all his days.

chunks.en: "I will sin and Yom Kippur will forgive,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: I will sin and Yom Kippur will atone for my sins,

chunks.en: Yom Kippur does not forgive.
chunks.st: Yom Kippur does not atone for his sins.

chunks.en: Sins between a person and Hashem,
chunks.st: Furthermore, for transgressions between a person and God,

words.note: HaMakom is a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: Yom Kippur forgives.
chunks.st: Yom Kippur atones;

chunks.en: Sins between a person and his friend,
chunks.st: however, for transgressions between a person and another,

chunks.en: Yom Kippur does not forgive,
chunks.st: Yom Kippur does not atone

chunks.en: until he makes up with his friend.
chunks.st: until he appeases the other person.

chunks.he: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,

chunks.st: Similarly, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya taught that point from the verse:

chunks.he: מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ (ויקרא טז),
chunks.en: "From all your sins, before Hashem you will be clean" (Vayikra 16).
chunks.st: “From all your sins you shall be cleansed before the Lord” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: Sins between a person and Hashem,
chunks.st: For transgressions between a person and God,

chunks.en: Yom Kippur forgives.
chunks.st: Yom Kippur atones;

chunks.en: Sins between a person and his friend,
chunks.st: however, for transgressions between a person and another,

chunks.en: Yom Kippur does not forgive,
chunks.st: Yom Kippur does not atone

chunks.en: until he makes up with his friend.
chunks.st: until he appeases the other person.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: In conclusion, Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "How lucky you are, Yisrael!
chunks.st: How fortunate are you, Israel;

chunks.en: Before Whom do you become pure,
chunks.st: before Whom are you purified,

chunks.en: and Who makes you pure?
chunks.st: and Who purifies you?

chunks.en: Your Father in Heaven,
chunks.st: It is your Father in Heaven,

chunks.en: as it says (Yechezkel 36),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: 'And I will sprinkle pure water on you, and you will be pure.'
chunks.st: “And I will sprinkle purifying water upon you, and you shall be purified” (Ezekiel 36:25).

chunks.en: And it says (Yirmiyahu 17),
chunks.st: And it says:

chunks.en: 'The mikveh of Yisrael is Hashem.'
chunks.st: “The ritual bath of Israel is God” (Jeremiah 17:13).

chunks.en: Just as a mikveh makes the tamei pure,
chunks.st: Just as a ritual bath purifies the impure,

chunks.he: אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְטַהֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל:
chunks.en: so too HaKadosh Baruch Hu makes Yisrael pure."
chunks.st: so too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, purifies Israel.
